1. These are the writ petitions under Article 226 of the Constitution of India wherein the petitioner is
Ashok vs Union Of India And 4 Others on 4 July, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54856766/
1

aggrieved by the order dated April 24, 2024 passed by the Divisional Railway Manager, Lucknow
and the subsequent impugned order dated April 27, 2024 passed by the Chief Catering Inspector,
Gorakhpur. 
2.  The case made out by the petitioner is that he has been carrying out the work as Commission Vendor since the year 1985. In earlier round of litigation, a co-ordinate Bench of this Court by order dated December 6, 2023 permitted the petitioner to continue with his retail snacks and tea shop on the Railway Platform provided he deposits the requisite commission as indicated in his licence. 
3. It is to be noted that during that period the petitioner was having appropriate certificate issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) which was valid till April 6, 2024. Upon expiry of the period of the said certificate, the impugned orders were passed by the respondents authorities wherein the petitioner was denied the right to continue with his retail snacks and tea shop on the Railway Platform. The reason provided in the impugned orders is dual in nature - firstly, it was stated that petitioner did not have the proper FSSAI certificate and secondly, it was stated that petitioner had attained the age of 60 years and therefore, could not continue as a Commission Vendor.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the ground taken in the impugned orders with regard to the age of the petitioner is completely arbitrary and is required to be rejected outright as the petitioner is not a Government employee and no age restriction applies to him. However, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner could not explain the reason for not having a valid FSSAI certificate. Neither the petitioner has made application in any manner before the FSSAI for issuance of certificate. 
5. In our view, without having a valid FSSAI certificate the petitioner cannot claim any right for carrying out the work as a Commission Vendor on the Railway Platform. 
6. Accordingly, the impugned orders cannot be interfered with and both the writ petitions are dismissed. 
7. However, we make it clear that in the event the FSSAI certificate is obtained by the petitioner from the authority concerned, he may apply to the Railways for allowing him to continue with his retail snacks and tea shop on the Railway Platform. The decision shall be taken by the Railways with regard to issue whether such a licence should be granted to the petitioner. 
Order Date :- 4.7.2024 Salim (Manjive Shukla, J.) (Shekhar B. Saraf, J.)
